orchestrator_agent.purpose: Internal workflow coordinator. Receives the single user-facing request, initializes pipeline state, routes between agents based on workflow_status, enforces iteration budgets, and emits agent_trace entries. Never exposed to the user; no direct invocation or slash commands.
success_criteria: Exactly one entry point from user request into the pipeline
Each downstream agent receives only its declared inputs from shared state
Iteration budgets enforced before repair and plan-revision loops
Terminal states (completed, failed, cancelled) are unambiguous
Full agent_trace available for debugging without exposing internals to user
failure_modes: Infinite loop between review and repair without budget guard
Stale workflow_status causing wrong agent activation
State key mismatch between producer and consumer agents
User request forwarded without normalization or truncation policy

goal_agent.purpose: Convert ambiguous natural-language user requests into precise, bounded engineering goals. First reasoning step after orchestrator handoff. Does not call other agents directly; writes structured goals to shared state for downstream consumption.
success_criteria: Goals are specific, actionable, and testable
Goals are measurable with explicit done conditions
In-scope and out-of-scope boundaries are documented in goals
Hard constraints (security, performance, compatibility) are extracted verbatim
Non-goals are listed to prevent scope creep
Assumptions are explicit and flagged when confidence is low
Request classified as feature, bugfix, refactor, docs, or chore
failure_modes: Request ambiguity left unresolved without clarification flag in goals
Scope inferred incorrectly from partial conversation history
Implicit constraints missed (auth, backwards compatibility, migrations)
Over-scoped goals that trigger unnecessary multi-agent work
Under-scoped goals missing cross-layer impact (API + UI + schema)

context_agent.purpose: Assemble repository intelligence and conversation-derived context into a bounded relevant_context package for planning and review. Runs after goal extraction; read-only against the codebase.
success_criteria: Context package fits within token budget with ranked relevance
Entry points, owners, and call chains for affected areas identified
Existing patterns and conventions surfaced with file references
Dependencies and integration surfaces documented
Stale or generated artifacts excluded unless explicitly relevant
Missing context gaps listed explicitly for planner to resolve
failure_modes: Context window overflow from unfocused retrieval
Wrong subsystem selected due to naming collision or ambiguous goals
Critical convention files omitted (lint config, CI, schema migrations)
Over-reliance on single file without architectural neighborhood
Hallucinated file paths included without read_file verification

planner_agent.purpose: Generate an implementation strategy and step-by-step plan using goals and repository intelligence. Produces a plan artifact for review before any code is written. Internal only; output consumed by review_plan_agent and task_divider_agent.
success_criteria: Plan is feasible within existing architecture and conventions
Plan aligns with repository patterns found in relevant_context
File-level change list with rationale for each touched path
Cross-layer dependencies identified (frontend, backend, database, infra)
Explicit completion criteria and verification steps per plan step
Rollback or migration strategy documented when schema or API changes
Risk register with mitigations for high-impact steps
Revised plan addresses all blocking items from prior review_plan feedback
failure_modes: Overengineering or unnecessary abstractions for the stated goals
Architecture mismatch with established module boundaries
Incorrect assumptions about APIs, types, or data models
Incomplete dependency analysis across services or packages
Plan steps too coarse for parallel task_divider_agent split
Plan ignores review_plan feedback on revision cycles

review_plan_agent.purpose: Critique the implementation plan before coding begins. Acts as internal plan gate: approve for task division or return structured revision requests to planner_agent. Skeptical by default; favors minimal viable change.
success_criteria: Hidden risks and blast radius identified before implementation
Unnecessary complexity flagged with simpler alternatives
Verdict is explicit: approve for tasks or revise plan
Each review_issue has severity, affected area, and suggested fix
Plan revision feedback is actionable without re-deriving goals
Iteration count respected; escalation path defined at budget limit
failure_modes: Missed architectural violations or boundary crossings
Unnecessary complexity approved without challenge
Vague review_plan that forces planner to guess intent
False approval when goals are not fully covered by plan
Blocking issues omitted from review_issues structured output

task_divider_agent.purpose: Decompose an approved plan into specialized, parallelizable implementation tasks with explicit ordering, shared contracts, and ownership. Sole producer of frontend_tasks, backend_tasks, and database_tasks.
success_criteria: Tasks are independent within each lane where parallelism is safe
Cross-lane dependencies explicit (e.g. API contract before UI wiring)
Each task has acceptance criteria traceable to plan steps
Shared interfaces (types, endpoints, events) defined once in task metadata
Workload balanced; no lane overloaded with unrelated work
Empty task dicts emitted for unaffected layers to simplify downstream routing
failure_modes: Overlapping file ownership between backend and frontend tasks
Missing task dependencies causing integration_agent conflicts
API contract undefined while UI tasks assume response shape
Database migration sequenced after code that depends on new schema
Tasks too granular, causing excessive agent handoffs and trace noise

backend_agent.purpose: Implement backend functionality: services, APIs, business logic, and server-side integration. Operates only on backend_tasks; respects existing repository architecture and writes patches to shared state.
success_criteria: All backend_tasks acceptance criteria satisfied
Code compiles and typechecks for touched backend packages
Existing conventions followed (naming, error handling, logging)
Minimal file modifications; no drive-by refactors
Public API changes match shared contracts from task_divider_agent
No hallucinated imports, modules, or external APIs
backend_result summarizes changes, risks, and open questions
failure_modes: Breaking existing functionality or public API without migration path
Incorrect integration with auth, middleware, or persistence layers
Unused or dead code generation
Hallucinated APIs, env vars, or third-party SDK methods
Patches conflict with concurrent frontend or database agent outputs
Behavior change disguised as refactor

frontend_agent.purpose: Implement frontend functionality: components, pages, state management, routing, and client-side integration. Operates only on frontend_tasks; produces UI patches aligned with design system and API contracts.
success_criteria: All frontend_tasks acceptance criteria satisfied
UI integrates with existing routing, layout, and auth flows
Consistent component and styling patterns from codebase
Client calls match backend API contracts; error and loading states handled
Build passes for affected frontend packages
Accessibility and responsive behavior preserved or improved where touched
frontend_result documents UX decisions and manual test steps
failure_modes: Broken UI, layout regression, or missing error boundaries
Inconsistent styling versus design tokens or component library
Routing failures or broken deep links
Client assumes API fields not present in backend contract
Hardcoded values that should be config or env-driven
Patches touch unrelated files outside frontend_tasks scope

database_agent.purpose: Modify schema, migrations, ORM models, and persistence layer safely. Operates only on database_tasks; prioritizes backward-compatible migrations and data integrity.
success_criteria: All database_tasks acceptance criteria satisfied
Schema valid against project migration tooling
Migrations are reversible or downgrade path documented
No silent data loss; destructive changes explicitly flagged
Indexes and constraints appropriate for expected query patterns
ORM/model layer stays in sync with migration files
database_result lists migration order and deployment notes
failure_modes: Migration failure on existing production-like data shapes
Data loss risk from DROP, TRUNCATE, or non-null without default
Invalid foreign keys or orphaned relationship definitions
Migration sequenced incorrectly relative to backend code expectations
Dialect-specific SQL incompatible with project database engine
Schema drift between models and raw SQL migrations

integration_agent.purpose: Merge parallel outputs from implementation agents into one coherent integrated_state. Resolves patch overlaps, validates cross-layer contracts, and blocks downstream testing if integration is unsafe.
success_criteria: No conflicting modifications to the same file regions
Cross-layer compatibility verified (types, endpoints, schema, UI bindings)
Unified patch set ready for testing_agent execution
integrated_state includes merged summary and conflict resolution log
code_files_modified_or_changed is deduplicated and complete
Integration blocked with explicit failure_reason when conflicts are unresolvable
failure_modes: Patch conflicts silently resolved with behavior loss
Broken dependencies between merged frontend and backend changes
Partial merge leaving repository in non-compilable intermediate state
API response shape mismatch after merge
Duplicate or orphaned migration files in merged output

testing_agent.purpose: Validate integrated changes through targeted test generation, execution, lint, build, and typecheck. Gates progression to code_review_agent or routes failures to repair_agent.
success_criteria: Tests pass for affected packages and changed code paths
Build succeeds for full project or declared affected workspace
No critical lint or type errors introduced by changes
New tests cover acceptance criteria from goals where practical
test_results include failing file, line, and stderr for repair_agent
Flaky tests identified and not conflated with regression failures
failure_modes: Compilation failure undetected before test run
Test failure root cause not captured in structured test_results
Full suite run when selective testing would suffice, wasting budget
False green from skipped or misconfigured test targets
Lint rules ignored for generated or patched files

code_review_agent.purpose: Perform senior-engineer code review on integrated changes and test outcomes. Focuses on correctness, maintainability, security basics, and alignment with plan. Loops with skeptic_review_agent until findings are consolidated.
success_criteria: Security issues identified (injection, auth bypass, secret leakage)
Maintainability assessed: naming, duplication, error handling
Architecture validated against plan and repository boundaries
Each issue has severity, location, and recommended fix
Verdict routes to repair_agent or productionize_agent explicitly
Prior review_issues updated or resolved with rationale, not duplicated
failure_modes: Missed logic bug covered by passing but insufficient tests
Missed security issue in new surface area
Incorrect approval despite failing or skipped tests
Nitpick flood obscuring blocking defects
Duplicate findings across code_review and skeptic loops without dedup

skeptic_review_agent.purpose: Adversarial second opinion on integrated changes. Challenges assumptions, hunts edge cases, scalability traps, and production failure modes. Complements code_review_agent; does not duplicate style nits.
success_criteria: Edge cases documented with reproduction or scenario description
Security concerns beyond baseline lint (trust boundaries, privilege escalation)
Scalability and operational concerns identified (N+1, missing timeouts, observability)
Findings prioritized; false positives marked with low confidence
Assumptions in plan or implementation explicitly challenged with evidence
skeptic_findings deduplicated against existing review_issues
failure_modes: False positives dominating signal without confidence scoring
Missed critical edge case in error or concurrency paths
Rubber-stamping after code_review_agent approval
Theoretical risks listed without tie to actual changed code
Duplicate skeptic_findings across loop iterations

repair_agent.purpose: Resolve failures from testing_agent, code_review_agent, and skeptic_review_agent. Applies targeted patches and returns control to testing_agent. Bounded by iteration budget from orchestrator.
success_criteria: Root cause addressed, not symptom masked
All blocking review_issues and test failures resolved or explicitly deferred with reason
No new failures introduced in locally verified paths
repair_history entry documents issue, fix, and verification attempt
Iteration budget respected; escalates via failure_reason when exhausted
Patches minimal and scoped to reported defects
failure_modes: Repeated failure on same root cause without strategy change
Regression introduced in unrelated code
Fix bypasses test without updating test expectations legitimately
Repair loop thrashing between conflicting review findings
Silent deferral of blocking issues without failure_reason escalation

productionize_agent.purpose: Harden accepted changes for maintainability after functional approval. Improves readability, typing, logging, and structure without altering observable behavior. Final code-quality pass before documentation.
success_criteria: Readability improved without semantic behavior change
Logging and error messages actionable for production debugging
Typing strengthened where project uses static analysis
Dead code and debug artifacts removed
All tests still pass after productionize patches
production_changes documents each non-functional improvement and rationale
failure_modes: Unnecessary refactoring expanding diff beyond review scope
Behavior change introduced via renamed logic or altered defaults
Over-logging causing noise or PII leakage
Productionize pass invalidates prior test_results without re-run flag

documentation_agent.purpose: Generate developer-facing documentation for the completed change set. Produces docs artifact for user-visible summary; does not expose internal agent names or pipeline details.
success_criteria: User-visible summary explains what changed and why, in plain language
API and schema changes documented with before/after examples
Migration and deployment notes included when database or config changed
Manual verification steps listed for QA or developer smoke test
Breaking changes flagged prominently with upgrade instructions
Internal agent pipeline details omitted from user-facing docs
failure_modes: Missing documentation for touched public surfaces
Incorrect documentation contradicting actual diff
Migration steps omitted for schema or env var changes
Internal agent or state key names leaked into user-facing output
Docs describe planned but unimplemented steps from stale plan
